notes: NOTHING CAN RE-STATE A MONTH YOU HAVE SIGNED OFF — NOT THE REGISTER, AND NOT AN IMPORT. The last release refused every act on the STATEMENT screen that would change a filed month, and left two ways round it. Both are now closed. THE CHEQUE AND LODGEMENT REGISTER IS GATED. This is the one that mattered most. The register is where cheques are actually ticked off, and marking one presented with CLEARED ON set to a date inside a filed month changes that month unpresented total, which is most of what the reconciliation says. It is the everyday action, not an exotic one, and the screen own advice — set Cleared on to the statement date you are working through — points straight at the date that does it. Ten acts in the register now go through the same gate, each on the date its own change turns on: marking a cheque presented or a lodgement credited, un-presenting or un-crediting one, reinstating a stale cheque, closing one against a journal, correcting a registered amount, deleting a hand-keyed cheque, and registering a cheque or lodgement dated into a filed month — because adding to a month outstanding list re-states it as surely as taking away. The refusal appears on the register screen in the same words, and the way back is the same: reopen that month on the Reconciliation screen. IMPORTING A STATEMENT IS GATED. LEFT THE BANK WITH NO CHEQUE and REACHED THE BANK WITH NO LODGEMENT are counted from a horizon: the earliest statement date you have ever imported for that account. Nothing before it is counted, which is what stops those schedules filling with every payment ever made the day you first import a statement. But importing a statement that reaches further back MOVES that horizon, and every qualifying ledger movement from the new date onward joins the schedules at once, in every month, including months already signed off. On one real set of books, importing the previous month statement would have moved a filed month by 974,536.35, and nothing on the screen would have said so. An import that would do this is now refused, before anything is written, so nothing is half-imported. The first statement you ever import for an account is checked the same way, because going from no horizon at all to a dated one is the same move. WHAT IS NOT REFUSED: re-importing the same statement, or importing one that covers the same period or a later one. Neither can move the horizon, so neither changes a filed month, and a guard that refused them would be crying wolf at ordinary work. Nor is importing lines that simply fall inside a filed month: that moves no figure on the reconciliation — the statement balance is typed, the cashbook comes from the ledger, the schedules come from the register — it only changes what a later sign-off would ask you to answer for. MATCHING NOW ASKS THE ITEMS, NOT ONLY THE LINE. Matching a statement line was gated on the bank date alone, which is right while every item being matched is still outstanding — and it always is. But that rested on four separate guards in three files, and the rule should not depend on all four staying as they are. Matching now asks each item whether it is already cleared and gates on the earliest date in play. Nothing you can do on the screen changes as a result; it is the rule standing on its own. INSTALLING: no data changes. This installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
